Triage: routed `domain:cli` (the decision surface is `packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts` + `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`) · type Feature (any code fix widens what the `/actions` envelope carries) → **`needs-user-decision`** (public contract shape — manual floor).

Premises (re-check before ruling):
- `resolveThrownHttpError` still builds `details` from a closed list and drops a thrown `.details` — `grep -n "const details" packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts`
- the trigger door still ships `errorMessage`/`summary` via `error.details` — `git grep -n "errorMessage" packages/runtime/src --include='*.ts'`
- both doors agree on `400 FLOW_FAILED` post-#9446 — re-run that card's paired-door check.

Four-facet analysis:
- **Platform long-term coherence**: Option B keeps the deliberately-narrowed shared resolver (#8016 / #9106) narrow — a typed refusal carrier recognised at the flow-action door is a closed, named channel; Option A is a general "any throw can ship wire payload" widening, the exact thing #9106 narrowed `code` to prevent. Option C freezes a declared-but-undelivered author message at the documented record-page door.
- **Measured business pull**: real — the console already reads `error.details.errorMessage` (objectui `flowResponse.ts`, #9414 / objectui#4899), and dispatching a flow through an ACTION is the documented way to expose it on a record page; today the author's failure text is silently replaced by the raw engine error.
- **AI-agent error-resistance**: A is the dangerous arm (silent wire-widening available to every thrower); B is closed-shape; C leaves a declared-but-unenforced key for agents to imitate.
- **Startup scope discipline**: B is bounded to one door and carries only the two fields the trigger door already ships; no new schema keys.

**Recommendation: B** — a typed refusal carrier that `dispatchFlowAction` throws and the `/actions` route recognises before the generic catch, carrying exactly `errorMessage` + `summary`; `resolveThrownHttpError` untouched. If ruled C instead, the deliverable becomes docs + the objectui reader stating the asymmetry, not code.

## The ruling — ⛔ not re-litigable

**Maintainer ruling recorded 2026-08-19**, verbatim authorization 「接受你的所有建议。」 (adopting the presented recommendation across an 11-card decision-inbox review):

**Option B — a typed refusal carrier.** `dispatchFlowAction` throws it; the `/actions` door recognises it **before** the generic catch and carries exactly two fields into `error.details` of the ADR-0112 envelope: **`errorMessage`** (the flow author's own failure text) and **`summary`** (the per-node run accounting).

- ⛔ **`resolveThrownHttpError` stays UNTOUCHED.** `packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts` is **out of surface**. The shared resolver's closed `details` list (#8016 / #9106) remains the rule for every other thrower, and Option A — a general "any throw may declare wire payload" widening — was **rejected by name** as the exact thing #9106 narrowed `code` to prevent.
- ⛔ **Option C rejected**: the console already reads `error.details.errorMessage` (objectui `flowResponse.ts`, #9414 / objectui#4899), and dispatching a flow through an ACTION is the documented record-page path.
- **Scope: bounded to the one door. No new schema keys.** Both doors keep agreeing on `400 FLOW_FAILED` post-#9446.

## ⛔ Hard boundary — the file the `/actions` route is registered in is HELD

⚠️ The `/actions` route registration lives at `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts:1385` (`server!.post(\`${base}/actions//:action\`, …)`), and **that file is held by sibling card #9813 this round** (same-file hard serial, maintainer-reaffirmed 2026-08-19).

⇒ The ruled fix should land in `action-execution.ts` + `domains/actions.ts` — the throw and the *handler-side* recognition — **not** in the route registration. **If you find the recognition genuinely has to happen inside `dispatcher-plugin.ts`, STOP and report.** ⛔ Do not edit it: sequencing the two cards is my call, not a widening you may take.

## Premise re-check before writing — triage's own commands

- `resolveThrownHttpError` still builds `details` from a closed list and **drops** a thrown `.details` — `grep -n "const details" packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts`
- the trigger door still ships `errorMessage`/`summary` via `error.details` — `git grep -n "errorMessage" packages/runtime/src --include='*.ts'`
- both doors still agree on `400 FLOW_FAILED` post-#9446 — re-run that card's paired-door check

⚠️ The card was written 2026-08-18 and `packages/runtime` has moved several times since (#9746, #9848 both landed in it today). ⛔ Treat every line reference as stale; locate by text.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure; falsifying them is a good run

- That a typed carrier can be recognised at the door **before** the generic catch without restructuring the catch. If the only way in is through the shared resolver, that contradicts the ruling — **stop and report the fork**, ⛔ do not quietly widen `resolveThrownHttpError`.
- That `errorMessage` and `summary` are available at the throw site with the same shape the trigger door ships. ⭐ **Pin the two doors against each other** — the card's whole point is that they diverge, so a test that only checks the `/actions` side would not notice them drifting apart again.

## Gates

Re-derive with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` from the **actually changed** paths. ⚠️ Three confirmed instances (#9721 / #9700) of it naming neither `pnpm lint` nor `check:slot-lookup` — run `pnpm lint` regardless. ⚠️ `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` is very likely implicated here — run it and report the reading. ⛔ Never weaken a gate.

Read verdicts from reported counts, ⛔ never a piped exit code. Report at draft-PR time. ⚠️ **Post the report as an issue comment on this card with the `os-dev-report` marker first, and read it back** — the terminal channel dropped two reports this shift and I wrongly treated both devs as dead.
